topic: Slope and rate of change --- finding and fixing inverted or sign-reversed slopes

traps.desc: inverted the ratio: put the change in x on top
inverted the ratio: change in x over change in y

problems.desc: Part (b): naming the error in Jonah's work. Full credit requires the student to say that Jonah put the change in x on top and the change in y underneath, that is, he inverted the slope ratio. Accept 'he used run over rise instead of rise over run' or 'the x differences belong on the bottom'. Do not accept 'he subtracted wrong' with no mention of which difference belongs on top.

traps.desc: subtracted the x-values in the opposite order from the y-values, reversing the sign

problems.desc: Part (b): naming the error in Mara's work. Full credit requires the student to say that Mara took the two differences in opposite orders, subtracting the first point's y from the second point's y but the second point's x from the first point's x, which flips the sign of the answer. Accept 'she started with a different point on the top and the bottom'. Do not accept 'she forgot the minus sign' alone, with no reference to the order of subtraction.

traps.desc: inverted the ratio: divided the change in hours by the change in gallons

problems.desc: Part (c): naming the error in Ravi's rate. Full credit requires the student to say that Ravi divided the change in hours by the change in gallons, so his ratio is upside down: the rate asked for is gallons per hour, so gallons must be on top. Accept an answer that says his units come out as hours per gallon. Do not accept 'he should have got a bigger number' with no reference to which quantity belongs on top.

traps.desc: inverted the rate: minutes per page instead of pages per minute

problems.desc: Part (b): naming the error in Sam's work. Full credit requires the student to say that Sam divided minutes by pages, which gives minutes per page, while the slope of pages against minutes needs pages on top. Accept an answer that checks the units and notices they come out reversed. Do not accept 'he divided wrong' with no statement of which quantity belongs on top.

traps.desc: took the y-difference in one order and the x-difference in the other, losing the negative

problems.desc: Part (b): naming the error in Aisha's work. Full credit requires the student to say that Aisha subtracted the y-values starting from the second point but the x-values starting from the first point, so her answer came out positive when the ramp falls from left to right and the slope must be negative. Accept an answer that argues from the direction of the ramp as long as the order of subtraction is named.

traps.desc: inverted the ratio: divided the change in tickets by the change in cost

problems.desc: Part (c): naming the error in Leo's slope. Full credit requires the student to say that Leo divided the change in tickets by the change in cost, inverting the ratio, and that dollars per ticket needs the dollar change on top. Accept a units argument: his answer is tickets per dollar. Do not accept a corrected number with no statement of what went wrong.

traps.desc: reversed the order of subtraction on the top only, flipping the sign

problems.desc: Part (b): explanation of which student is right and what the other did. Full credit requires the student to say that Dana is right and that Kofi subtracted the y-values in the reverse order from the x-values, which flips the sign. Accept supporting evidence that the line falls from left to right because y drops while x rises, so the slope must be negative. Do not accept a choice with no reason.
